claims.text: Increasing Cr content relative to equiatomic FeNiCrCoCu enhances formation of a Cr-rich oxide layer during high-temperature sliding.
The Cr-rich oxide layer reduces direct metallic contact at the sliding interface.
The Cr-rich oxide layer suppresses dislocation nucleation.
Cr enrichment decreases the overall wear rate relative to the equiatomic coating.
Cr enrichment decreases microscopic deformation relative to the equiatomic coating.
Temperatures above approximately 600 °C are sufficiently high to promote dynamic oxide formation during wear.
Enhanced Cr content promotes rapid formation of a continuous Cr-rich oxide film during high-temperature sliding.
Enhanced Cr content promotes formation of an adherent Cr-rich oxide film during high-temperature sliding.
The oxide film hinders dislocation motion in the underlying FeNiCrCoCu matrix.
The oxide film suppresses slip events in the underlying FeNiCrCoCu matrix.
The Cr-enriched coating will have lower wear volume than the equiatomic coating.
The Cr-enriched coating will have lower friction than the equiatomic coating.
The Cr-enriched coating will exhibit fewer or less pronounced slip bands than the equiatomic coating.
The predicted oxide-mediated behavior requires oxygen access.
Under inert atmospheres or at substantially lower temperatures, the proposed oxide-mediated mechanism may not operate.
Prior studies of compositional tuning in this specific high-entropy alloy system under dynamic sliding conditions are limited.
